description: Org-wide Renovate preset. Consumed by a one-line renovate.json in each repo:
{ "extends": ["local>quynhonsemiconductor/.github:renovate-config"] }
PRIVATE PACKAGE ACCESS IS NOT CONFIGURED HERE, and looking for it in this file
is the obvious mistake. Renovate reads @quynhonsemiconductor/* from GitHub
Packages, which is a private scope its installation token does not cover — it
reported 'no-result' for all five packages and silently proposed no updates
for them. The fix is a HOST RULE bound in the Mend Developer Portal UI
(Settings > Credentials > Host Rules): npm.pkg.github.com, hostType npm,
using the GITHUB_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN secret — a read:packages classic PAT
belonging to the qnsc-bot machine account.
A hostRules block WAS tried here first, referencing the secret as
{{ secrets.GITHUB_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN }}. It did not resolve on the hosted
app — app.renovatebot.com/encrypt now states config-based secrets are
superseded by UI-managed ones. It is removed rather than left in place,
because config that looks load-bearing and is not costs the next reader more
than no config at all.
Symptom if the token lapses: Dependency Lookup Warnings reappear on the Mend
dashboard, no PRs are opened for the five first-party packages, and nothing
fails.

pinDigests=true: every update pins to a commit digest; git refs (the shared ci reusables) carry the release in the trailing # vX.Y.Z comment, which Renovate rewrites on bump. This is what retires the moving v1 tag for good: pipelines change only through reviewed Renovate PRs.
REBASING IS DELIBERATELY LAZY (rebaseWhen=conflicted, updateNotScheduled=false).
main-protection requires branches to be up to date, and Renovate's default rebaseWhen=auto
reads that as 'rebase whenever behind', while updateNotScheduled defaults to true, which lets
those rebases happen OUTSIDE the Monday schedule. Together: every push to main re-pushed every
open Renovate branch and re-ran its full CI. Measured 2-16 Oct on rova: 1,729 of 3,116 workflow
runs were Renovate's, from 8 branches, most started within 15 minutes of a push to main.
A Renovate branch now updates only when it conflicts. The merge tooling brings a branch up to
date at merge time, which is what the strict policy needs.
AUTOMERGE HAS TWO PRECONDITIONS THIS FILE CANNOT SET. (1) The Renovate app must be allowed to
merge under main-protection: it requires one approving code-owner review and the only bypass
actor is the Admin role, so today no Renovate PR has ever been merged by the bot (the last 9 on
rova were all merged by a person). (2) With rebaseWhen=conflicted and a strict up-to-date rule,
a PR that falls behind main without conflicting is not auto-mergeable until someone updates it
(documented Renovate behaviour). Until (1) is decided, the automerge rules are inert and
harmless: the PR still opens, still runs CI, and is merged by hand.

packageRules.description: Group non-major npm updates into one PR per dependency type, mirroring the Dependabot policy this replaces. config:recommended separates majors already but does NOT group anything, so without this a handover from Dependabot trades two grouped PRs a week for one PR per dependency.
Same, for dev dependencies — kept separate so a dev-tool bump never sits in the same PR as a runtime one.

Majors are labelled and never auto-merged. Separation is already guaranteed: config:recommended sets separateMajorMinor, and the grouping rules above match only minor and patch, so a major can never land inside one of those PRs. This rule deliberately does NOT force groupName off — it would override the shared-CI grouping below, which is intended even for a major of our own actions. Why it matters: four grouped-major PRs were opened across rova and opshub in one week (NestJS 11 to 12 across nine packages plus ioredis 5 to 6; TypeScript 6 to 7 with vitest 4 to 5) and all four were closed unreviewed, because a 45-package diff containing a framework major cannot be attributed when something breaks.
Group shared CI (reusables + composite actions) into one PR
Auto-merge patch bumps of pinned GitHub Actions once checks pass minimumReleaseAge 3 days, like the other automerge rules: a hijacked action release is the same supply-chain path.

description: tf-modules: the org's shared Terraform modules, consumed as git tags pinned PER MODULE
(source = git::https://github.com/quynhonsemiconductor/tf-modules.git//modules/cache?ref=cache-v1.1.0).
WITHOUT this rule Renovate proposes NOTHING for them, silently. The tags are not semver —
`cache-v1.1.0` has a module prefix — so default versioning cannot parse them, and a
dependency Renovate cannot version is one it skips rather than one it reports. 'No PRs'
then reads as 'nothing to update', which is why this went unnoticed: rova, opshub and
qnsc-kb-backend all pin tf-modules by tag and not one has ever received a bump for it,
while infra (which carried this rule privately) has.
The `compatibility` capture group is the module prefix, so Renovate only ever proposes
updates WITHIN one module's tag series — cache-* can never bump to secrets-*.
Lifted here from infra/renovate.json, which is where it was written and where it worked.
It belongs at org level because five repos consume tf-modules this way, not one.

packageRules.description: One PR for every GitHub Actions update (pins, digests, and the shared CI reusables), instead of one PR per action. Eight Renovate branches were each rebased on every push to main; a single group is one branch. Declared after the 'shared CI' rule on purpose: a later match overwrites groupName, so shared CI joins this group rather than keeping its own.

Auto-merge non-major dev dependencies and digest pins once required checks are green. Majors are excluded by matchUpdateTypes, so this cannot override the major rule above. See the note at the top of this file about what actually has to be true for an automerge to land under main-protection. minimumReleaseAge 3 days: dev dependencies (vite, TypeScript, bundlers) are compiled into the web bundle, so a hijacked patch release would take exactly this path; a few days is the window in which the registry usually yanks one.
Auto-merge digest pins (GitHub Actions SHAs, Docker image digests) once required checks are green. minimumReleaseAge 3 days for the same reason: a hijacked digest or tag is the supply-chain path.

Never auto-merge the shared CI reusables: they carry the required-check names, and a bump is a decision. A group automerges only when EVERY update in it does, so a PR that contains a shared CI bump is left for a person. DECLARED AFTER the automerge rules on purpose: Renovate applies packageRules in order and a later match overwrites field by field, so this has to come last among them to win for a shared-CI digest (which the digest rule would otherwise automerge).

Data stores move as ONE PR: PostgreSQL, pgvector and Valkey images in compose files and CI service containers are grouped, so a bump is reviewed against the same version table in docs/TECH_STACK.md. Minor and patch only; a major is its own decision and is never automerged. Terraform's engine_version is NOT in this group: it is bumped by hand in the same change, and each repository's consistency test enforces the major against compose.
Valkey stays on the 8.1 line. ElastiCache's '8.2' is open-source 8.1 plus valkey-search, and no valkey/valkey:8.2 image exists, so a 9.x or 8.2 tag is never proposed.
PostgreSQL stays on the 18 line (RDS major 18). A 19 tag is a major decision and is never proposed.
pgvector tags are <extension>-pg<major> (0.8.2-pg18), so the line is the pg suffix, not a leading 18. Stays on PostgreSQL 18.

First-party packages: their own group, never auto-merged. They are published from app-platform by this org and released together, so a bump to them is a platform decision — burying one in a group with a third-party patch loses that signal. THIS RULE MUST STAY LAST. Renovate applies packageRules in order and a later match overwrites an earlier one field by field. While this rule sat FIRST, the generic 'npm production (non-major)' rule above matched the same packages and overwrote its groupName, so @quynhonsemiconductor/identity and platform-cache were both proposed inside a 46-package third-party group in rova and opshub — the exact outcome this rule exists to prevent. It was invisible because the group PR is still opened and still green; only the dashboard's package list shows where they ended up.
